sources.citation: De Wolf AM, Van Zundert TC, De Cooman S, Hendrickx JF. Theoretical effect of hyperventilation on speed of recovery and risk of rehypnotization following recovery - a Gas Man simulation. BMC Anesthesiology. 2012;12:22.
sources.note: Table 1 reports the Gas Man sevoflurane blood:gas and tissue:gas coefficients used here.

sources.citation: Strum DP, Eger EI II. Partition coefficients for sevoflurane in human blood, saline, and olive oil. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1987;66(7):654-656.
sources.note: Primary human study reporting a blood:gas coefficient of 0.686 +/- 0.047 at 37 degrees C. Version 0.1.0 uses 0.65 to match the standard Gas Man parameter set.

sources.citation: Yasuda N, Targ AG, Eger EI II. Solubility of I-653, sevoflurane, isoflurane, and halothane in human tissues. Anesthesia & Analgesia. 1989;69(3):370-373.
sources.note: Primary human-tissue partition-coefficient study underlying the tissue-solubility model.

sources.citation: Drager Vapor 2000 Sevoflurane vaporizer specification: calibrated concentration range 0.2-8%.
sources.note: Standard variable-bypass sevoflurane vaporizer (e.g. Drager Vapor 2000, Datex-Ohmeda Sevotec 5) calibrated dial maximum, used here as max_delivered_concentration_percent. This is a device-capability limit on the delivered-concentration control, not a scientific model parameter; it does not affect the governing equations.

sources.citation: Nickalls RWD, Mapleson WW. Age-related iso-MAC charts for isoflurane, sevoflurane and desflurane in man. British Journal of Anaesthesia. 2003;91(2):170-174.
sources.note: MAC is age-dependent; this project's reference-adult model has no age parameter, so mac_percent uses the flat adult value from De Wolf et al. above (same paper already cited for partition coefficients: 'MAC values that we used in our Gas Man simulations are: desflurane 6%, sevoflurane 2%, isoflurane 1.2%'), not an age-adjusted one. Used as the controller's starting delivered-concentration default (1 MAC), not a governing-equation parameter.
